bugs.title: Async request event is saved without include_in_calculations
bugs.description: When the payment app answers a refund or charge request with only a PSP reference (async flow), the request event is saved with include_in_calculations left at its default, False. calculate_transaction_amount_based_on_events excludes such events, so the requested amount never moves into the pending field.
mechanism_anchors: the calculation excludes events with include_in_calculations=False
async flow returns only a PSP reference, no event
the sync path (create_transaction_event_for_transaction_session) sets the flag; this path does not
bugs.fix: Set the request event's include_in_calculations flag to True when it is updated with the PSP reference (upstream PR #14380).

grader_instructions: Task-only example built from a real upstream bug. The multiple-choice parts are graded exactly; no judge is needed.
Upstream: issue saleor/saleor#14327, fixed by PR #14380.

distractors.where.a: the filter is intended: failure events are created with the flag off precisely so they are not counted
distractors.where.c: the refund amount is right ($10.00); the problem is how it is counted afterwards
distractors.where.d: this rule is correct; it never sees the request event because the event is filtered out earlier
distractors.why.a: the pending amount comes from the request event, not a success event; it would show as pending if the request were counted
distractors.why.c: the transaction item is saved separately with update_fields; the request event save does not touch it
distractors.why.d: the PSP reference is stored on the line just before the save
distractors.fix.a: failure events (create_failed_transaction_event) and other non-amount events would start counting and corrupt the totals
distractors.fix.b: the request would stay pending forever, even after the provider confirms success
distractors.fix.d: response events are already created with the flag on; the request event is the one left out
